title: Headcount Growth and Restoration Reserves: Paystride Payroll Card Program Training Notes
content:
**What does headcount growth change when a restoring payment is worked out for a Paystride Payroll Card Program?**
The restoration batch basis — the batch figure the restoration reserve is taken on — is multiplied for headcount growth by comparing the cards loaded by the most recent regular payroll batch, the one with the latest pay date, with the average cards per regular payroll batch posted in the restoration look-back, their card counts summed and divided by their number:

- at least 1.1 times that average — by 1.1;
- at least 1.05 times but less than 1.1 times — by 1.05;
- less than 1.05 times, or with no regular payroll batch in the look-back — the basis is not multiplied for growth.

**Which batches enter the average?** The regular payroll batches posted in the restoration look-back holding the funding entries dated today or earlier that lie fewer than three whole months before today, the whole months between two dates being the difference in calendar months less one when the later date's day of the month is smaller than the earlier date's. The most recent regular batch is taken by its pay date, whichever batch that is.

**What are the cards of a batch?** The cards loaded by that payroll batch, as the batch entry records them.

**Worked comparisons (hypothetical; an average of 200 cards per regular batch in the look-back)**

| Cards loaded by the most recent regular batch | Times the average | Multiplier of the restoration batch basis |
|---|---|---|
| 221 | 1.105 | 1.05 |
| 220 | 1.10 | 1.1 |
| 210 | 1.05 | 1.05 |
| 209 | 1.045 | none |

**A figure on the basis (hypothetical).** A restoration batch basis of 9,640.00 with the most recent batch at 1.12 times the average becomes 10,604.00; at 1.06 times the average it becomes 10,122.00.
